I need to recall ECCN 3A090 as amended by the October 2023 rule (88 FR 73458).

3A090.a: Integrated circuits with one or more digital processing units having either:
a.1. A TPP of 4800 or more; or
a.2. A TPP of 1600 or more and performance density of 5.0 or more.

3A090.b: Integrated circuits (not meeting a) with:
b.1. TPP of 2400 or more but less than 4800 and performance density of 1.6 or more but less than 5.5; or
b.2. TPP of 1600 or more and performance density of 3.0 or more but less than 5.0 (hmm, I should check this against the actual text). The actual text:

b.1. A TPP of 2400 or more and less than 4800 and a performance density of 1.6 or more and less than 5.5; or
b.2. A TPP of 1600 or more, and a performance density of 3.0 or more and less than 5.0 (the final rule had "TPP of 1600 or more and PD 3.0 or more but less than 5.0")... Plus b.3 added for the 3A090.b note on 'not designed or marketed for datacenters' - actually the datacenter distinction applies to the license requirements and the NAC/ACA notes, not to the ECCN paragraphs. The ECCN 3A090.a and .b are defined purely by parameters.

Now applying: TPP 3000, PD 2.5.
- a.1: needs TPP ≥ 4800. No.
- a.2: TPP ≥ 1600 and PD ≥ 5.0. No.
- b.1: TPP 2400 to <4800 and PD 1.6 to <5.5. TPP 3000 is in range, PD 2.5 is in range. Yes.
- b.2: PD ≥ 3.0 required. No.

The datacenter design/marketing matters for license exception and for 3A090.c in some contexts, but 3A090.b.1 as an ECCN classification is parameter-based. In the 2023 rule, 3A090.b was not limited to datacenter chips; the datacenter factor affects the license requirements (e.g., the 4A090/ .z and the NAC notifications and the license exception ACA). Actually, I recall the 2023 rule's 3A090.b.1 text: "A TPP of 2400 or more and less than 4800 and a 'performance density' of greater than or equal to 1.6 and less than 5.5" with no datacenter qualifier. The datacenter qualifier appears in the 3A090.a reference to the license requirements paragraph (§742.6(a)(6)), where non-datacenter chips under b get notification rather than license. So the chip is covered by b.1.

Every threshold is above 5 × 10^24 FLOPs: California SB 53 and the amended New York RAISE Act use 10^26, the EU Article 51(2) presumption uses 10^25, and the ECCN 4E091 heading uses 10^26. The model's cumulative training compute of 5 × 10^24 falls short of all four, so it satisfies none of them on compute alone.

Thresholds as I recall them:

- California SB 53 defines a "frontier model" as one trained with more than 10^26 FLOPs. The model's 5 x 10^24 is below that, so it fails.
- The amended New York RAISE Act, as signed with chapter amendments, follows SB 53 and uses 10^26 FLOPs. It fails.
- EU AI Act Article 51(2) presumes a general-purpose model has high-impact capabilities when cumulative training compute exceeds 10^25 FLOPs. The model's 5 x 10^24 is below that, so it fails.
- ECCN 4E091, from the January 2025 AI diffusion rule, covers model weights of models trained with more than 10^26 operations. It fails too. (That rule was rescinded, but the question asks only about the heading's compute test.)

The model is at 5 x 10^24, which is below every threshold, so it satisfies none of the four tests.

The case-by-case policy in the rule covers chips below both thresholds (TPP under 21,000 and total DRAM bandwidth under 6,500 GB/s). With a TPP of exactly 21,000, this chip fails the "less than" test, so the rule's case-by-case path does not apply and the presumption of denial for China and Macau governs.

I'm recalling the January 2026 BIS rule, "Revision to License Review Policy for Advanced Computing Commodities" (91 FR 1684), which created a case-by-case review policy for certain chips exported to China and Macau (destinations in Country Group D:5 and Macau). From memory, the conditions were: TPP less than 21,000 and total DRAM bandwidth less than 6,500 GB/s, plus the paragraph (dd) certifications (commercial availability in the US, security procedures, no reduction of US supply, and so on).

The question gives TPP of exactly 21,000 and bandwidth of 5,900 GB/s. If the rule requires TPP less than 21,000, then exactly 21,000 fails the threshold and the default presumption of denial applies. My recollection of the text of 742.6(b)(10)(iii)(A)(1) is that it covers items with a TPP "less than 21,000" and total DRAM bandwidth "less than 6,500 GB/s". The question says to treat every figure as exact, which suggests the boundary matters, and 21,000 sits right at the boundary. So the chip is not eligible for case-by-case review.

Answer: B
